new_statements.quote: 3.9. Acentuación. En la mayoría de los casos, el acento recae en la penúltima sílaba (véase 4.6); por ejemplo: (16) [míkuy] '¡come!' (17) [mikúyan] 'están comiendo' (18) [mikukúlkuy] '¡cómelo todo!' [p. 20] ... 4.6. Interjecciones. Las interjecciones reciben el acento en la última sílaba (véase 3.9) y son las siguientes: atratráw '¡qué miedo!' alaláw '¡qué frío!' akacháw grito de quemadura/picazón ananáw '¡ayayay!' [p. 32] ... 3.8.2. Apócope. Ciertos sufijos de forma -CV experimentan opcionalmente la pérdida de vocal final lo que ocasiona un cambio de acentuación. Entre esos sufijos están /-mi/ 'directo', /-shi/ 'reportativo', /-tri/ 'conjetura' y /-si/ 'también'. Por ejemplo: (4) ima-ta-mi → [imatámi]/[imátam] [p. 18]
new_statements.translation: 3.9 Stress. In most cases the stress falls on the penultimate syllable (see 4.6); for example: [míkuy] 'eat!', [mikúyan] 'they are eating', [mikukúlkuy] 'eat it all up!' ... 4.6 Interjections. Interjections take the stress on the final syllable (see 3.9) and are the following: atratráw 'how frightening!', alaláw 'how cold!', akacháw (cry of burning/itching), ananáw 'ouch!' ... 3.8.2 Apocope. Certain suffixes of the shape -CV optionally lose their final vowel, which causes a change of stress. Among these suffixes are /-mi/ 'direct', /-shi/ 'reportative', /-tri/ 'conjecture' and /-si/ 'also'. For example: ima-ta-mi → [imatámi]/[imátam].
new_statements.citation: Wroughton, John R. 1996. Gramática y textos del quechua Shausha Huanca. Documento de Trabajo No. 30. Pucallpa: Ministerio de Educación / Instituto Lingüístico de Verano.
new_statements.locator: sec. 3.9 Acentuación, printed p. 20 (PDF p. 22); also sec. 4.6 Interjecciones, p. 32 (PDF p. 34) and sec. 3.8.2 Apócope, p. 18 (PDF p. 20)
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is on the penultimate syllable of the phonological word (root plus suffixes, including enclitic-like evidential/additive suffixes), with no weight sensitivity mentioned (vowel length exists but plays no stated role). Interjections are stressed on the final syllable. When an evidential or additive -CV suffix optionally drops its vowel, the stress stays on what was the penult of the full form, so the apocopated word surfaces with antepenultimate-looking stress ([imátam], [chaypítash], [manáchutr]).
new_statements.exceptions: Interjections (atratráw, alaláw, akacháw, ananáw) have final stress; apocopated forms of -mi/-shi/-tri/-si show a shifted stress ([imatámi] ~ [imátam]). 'En la mayoría de los casos' signals other unspecified exceptions.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level; examples are fully suffixed words in phonetic brackets (citation forms and text forms); data from Ricrán and Molinos districts, prov. Jauja, 1986-87.
new_statements.identity_note: Wroughton 1996 describes exactly the Jauja (Shausha/Shawsha) Wanka variety = jauj1238 [qxw]; data from Ricrán and Molinos districts, prov. Jauja, dept. Junín (1986-87). Wroughton (p. 12, citing Cerrón-Palomino) notes Shausha is the most conservative of the three Wanka subdialects (Shausha, Huaycha, Huaylla; the latter two = huay1241 Huaylla Wanca Quechua [qvw]). The 1976 Cerrón-Palomino grammar covers the Wanka supralect as a whole.
